key_insight: STITCH grounds agent memory by indexing each trajectory step with a structured retrieval cue called contextual intent, enabling retrieval that matches the agent’s latent goal rather than surface-level entities — reducing context-mismatched evidence in long-horizon interactions.
problem_solved: Memory retrieval in long-horizon, goal-oriented interactions often returns context-mismatched facts because similar entities recur under different latent goals; STITCH addresses this by making memory retrieval intent-aware.
method: Index each trajectory step with a structured retrieval cue (contextual intent) that captures the latent goal and constraints of that step.
Retrieve historical steps by matching the current step’s contextual intent (intent-aware retrieval) instead of relying on surface entity similarity.
Integrate intent-indexed retrieval into the agent’s memory pipeline so actions consult goal-aligned history during decision-making.
impact: Makes LLM-based agents more reliable in long-horizon, multi-goal tasks by improving relevance of retrieved memory and reducing errors from spurious context matches — enabling better planning, troubleshooting, and evaluation.
visual_elements: Timeline/sequence diagram: trajectory steps labeled with structured retrieval cues and contextual intents to show how indexing works over time.
Retrieval flowchart: compare intent-matched retrieval vs naive entity-based retrieval, highlighting correct vs mismatched evidence returned.
Before/after bar chart: relative improvement in retrieval relevance or downstream task consistency when using STITCH (conceptual comparison).
Icon set: memory (stacked cards), intent (target/compass), and goal (flag) to reinforce the core components.
paper_title: Grounding Agent Memory in Contextual Intent
paper_authors: Ruozhen Yang, Yucheng Jiang, Yueqi Jiang, Priyanka Kargupta, Yunyi Zhang
